paragraphs: Hyman lists Rav Acha bar Hoshaya in the Rosh at the beginning of Eruvin chapter 1, Rav Chama bar Oshaya in Sanhedrin 25a, Yehudah bar Oshaya in Eruvin 80a, Marinus bar Oshaya in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:5, Rav Nachman bar Oshaya in Shabbat 65a, and Rav Natan bar Oshaya in Shabbat 81b.

notes.text: The work printed שת beside Rav Nachman’s citation has not been securely identified.

The saved whole Davidson Shabbat65a scalar explicitly has full Rav Nachman bar Oshaya reporting Rabbi Yochanan, supporting the Shabbat match alongside supplied שת. This does not prove a dropped bet in Hyman’s printed or transcribed text. Heading Oshaya and first-body Hoshaya remain different supplied forms; ב״א is completed contextually from the entry, not an authority binding. Full Rav titles are supplied, and Marinus/Yehudah gain no new title. The other citations and Rosh beginning-chapter1 were not newly inspected.

The printed notice reads Berakhot 6:5 and Shabbat 65a, where the supplied transcription has 1:5 and שת. The Rosh, Eruvin 1:4, quotes a Jerusalem Talmud passage naming Rabbi Acha bar Oshaya. The consulted Sanhedrin 25a calls Chama Rabbi, and Eruvin 80a calls Yehudah Rav. Shabbat 65a and 81b name Rav Nachman and Rav Natan respectively. At Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:5 Guggenheimer’s Hebrew reads Marinus bei Rabbi Yehoshua, which he translates as a patronymic of Rabbi Joshua. His note reports the Oshaya form in other occurrences. The list gives occurrences of the patronymic without establishing a shared father.
